abstract: We prove an $X^{3/4+\epsilon}$ bound for smoothed normalized quartic Gauss sums over Gaussian primes, with logarithmic prime weight, for every fixed integer angular type. The published fixed-angular exponent of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin is $5/6$. We use the exponent-one square-parameter mean proved earlier by David, Devin, Fazzari and Waxman, in the normalized-level formulation recorded in Paper 106, and extend it to angular type zero by retaining the theta residue using Suzuki's square relation. The prime extraction uses a smooth hyperbola partition of $\Lambda=\mu*\log$. Multiplication by the Möbius function conjugates the normalized Gauss coefficient and reflects its angular index, so both hyperbola halves become level sums with level at most a constant times $\sqrt X$. A common Mellin integral separates the moving cutoff; an explicit finite smooth-profile seminorm controls the resulting family uniformly. The averaged level estimate then bounds both halves by $X^{3/4+\epsilon}$, without a Type-II estimate. The mean prediction, Gauss-square formula, quadratic large sieve and classical hyperbola method are credited to their sources. A standalone CPU supplement checks the finite Gauss, divisor and cutoff identities, separately from the analytic proof. We obtain no prime asymptotic, optimal angular or height uniformity, estimate uniform in a growing odd numerator, mixed zero-detector saving or new zero-free region. The Riemann hypothesis remains unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Correct the omitted attribution to David–Devin–Fazzari–Waxman, arXiv:2608.06286v1 Proposition 8.3, and distinguish its prior mean from this paper's hyperbola prime theorem. Define primary explicitly, describe the phase correction mathematically, and explain the consequence of the existing prime symmetry for the conjectural angular bias. No theorem, proof estimate, or supplement code is changed. Normalize LaTeX escaping in the metadata abstract.
title: A three-quarter bound for smoothed quartic Gauss sums over Gaussian primes
